title: The plastic shopping bag, 1933–2018, and world plastic production 1950–2019

facts.text: Polyethylene, the most widely used plastic, was first made in an industrially practical way in 1933, by accident, at a chemical plant in Northwich, England.
The British military first used polyethylene in secret during World War II.
In 1965 the Swedish company Celloplast patented a one-piece polyethylene shopping bag designed by its engineer Sten Gustaf Thulin.
By 1979 plastic bags held 80 percent of the bag market in Europe (four out of every five bags).
In 1982 the U.S. supermarket chains Safeway and Kroger switched to plastic bags, and other stores followed.
By the end of the 1980s plastic bags had almost completely replaced paper bags around the world.
Plastic bags have been found from the deep ocean to the summit of Mount Everest and the polar ice.
In 1997 the sailor and researcher Charles Moore discovered the Great Pacific Garbage Patch, a huge area of floating plastic waste.
In 2002 Bangladesh became the first country to ban thin plastic bags, after they were found to have clogged drains during disastrous floods.
As of July 2018, UNEP found that 127 of the 192 countries it reviewed had some national law on plastic bags.
World plastic production was about 2 million tonnes in 1950 and about 459.7 million tonnes in 2019, roughly 230 times as much.
facts.note: 倍數為衍生數字：459.746016 ÷ 2 ≈ 229.9，文中寫 around 230 times

facts.text: World plastic production was about 17 million tonnes in 1965, about 73 million tonnes in 1982 and about 231 million tonnes in 2002.
